question: Is Apple's balance sheet healthy? Look at liquidity, debt and net cash.

answer.summary: Apple's FY2023 balance sheet is solvent and deleveraging: the company held net cash of $51.01B (negative net debt) at 2023-09-30, up from $49.04B a year earlier [F01425][F01424]. Total debt fell 7.5% YoY to $111.09B [F01423] and debt/equity dropped 24.6% to 1.79x [F01427], while cash rose 26.7% to $29.96B [F00091] and short-term investments rose 28.1% to $31.59B [F00093]. Liquidity is the main caveat: the current ratio improved from 0.88x to 0.99x but remained below 1.0x in both years, with current assets of $143.57B [F00103] still under current liabilities of $145.31B [F00125]. Interest coverage remains high at 29.06x but fell 28.7% YoY from 40.75x [F01432]. Noncurrent marketable securities declined 16.8% to $100.54B [F00105], partially offsetting the cash build in the net-cash calculation.
drivers: Net cash position widened from $49.04B to $51.01B (+4.0% YoY) [F01425]: total debt fell 7.5% to $111.09B [F01423] and cash rose 26.7% to $29.96B [F00091], partly offset by noncurrent marketable securities falling 16.8% to $100.54B [F00105].
Current ratio improved 0.88x -> 0.99x (+12.4% YoY) [F01421] as current assets grew 6.0% to $143.57B [F00103] while current liabilities fell 5.6% to $145.31B [F00125].
Debt/equity decreased 24.6% (2.37x -> 1.79x) [F01427], reflecting the lower total debt of $111.09B [F01423].
Interest coverage fell 28.7% YoY (40.75x -> 29.06x) [F01432], coinciding with the FY2023 operating income decline of 4.3% ($119.44B -> $114.30B) [F00037].
Within debt, long-term noncurrent debt fell 3.7% to $95.28B [F00127] and current portion of long-term debt fell 11.7% to $9.82B [F00123].
risks_and_red_flags: Liquidity: current ratio below 1.0x in both FY2022 (0.88x) [F01420] and FY2023 (0.99x) [F01421] - current liabilities exceed current assets.
Interest coverage dropped 29% to 29.06x in FY2023 [F01432]; still strong but a marked decline from 40.75x in FY2022 [F01431].
Inventory grew 28% in FY2023 while cost of revenue fell 4% [F00099][F00022] - potential build-up risk.
Operating cash flow fell 9.5% ($122.15B -> $110.54B) in FY2023 [F00224].
Shareholder payouts of $92.58B (dividends + buybacks) were 93% of free cash flow of $99.58B in FY2023 [F01448][F01389], leaving little room to absorb a downturn.
The Company is exposed to credit risk and fluctuations in the values of its investment portfolio [T00225].

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 actuals show a solvent, deleveraging balance sheet: net cash of $51.01B [F01425], total debt down 7.5% to $111.09B [F01423], debt/equity of 1.79x [F01427], and interest coverage of 29.06x [F01432]; the weak spot is the sub-1.0x current ratio of 0.99x [F01421].
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: Management believes its cash, cash equivalents and unrestricted marketable securities, which totaled $148.3 billion as of September 30, 2023, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond [T00350] - this is forward-looking management belief, not an actual.

Verify the composition and maturity schedule of the $111.09B total debt [F01423], including commercial paper reliance.
Investigate the 28% inventory growth against a 4% cost-of-revenue decline [F00099][F00022] for build-up or obsolescence risk.
Decompose the interest-coverage decline (40.75x -> 29.06x [F01432]) into operating income (-4.3% [F00037]) versus interest expense movements.
